clue.text: Beams put up while talking

indicators.note: spoken words are heard rather than read, so the letters follow the sound

parts.note: to put up something is to raise it

explanation.surface: Someone holds up girders while chatting on a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are narrow beams of light or other radiation.

clue.text: Elimination of radiation covering cricket ground

indicators.note: in a down clue the radiation unit sits on top of the ground

parts.note: the rem is a unit of radiation dose
the Oval is a London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Fallout spreads over a cricket pitch and a clean-up follows.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a Test cricket ground in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Removal is the act of getting rid of something, an elimination.

clue.text: Rustic couple left

parts.note: a yoke couples two oxen together

explanation.surface: A country pair has departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country person, a rustic.

clue.text: He maintains discipline among members — but not with this

definitions.text: He maintains discipline among members — but not with this

parts.words: He maintains discipline among members — but not with this
parts.note: a parliamentary officer who keeps MPs voting with their party shares his title with a lash, which he never actually uses on them

explanation.surface: A party official keeps MPs in line without resorting to a lash.
explanation.definitionFit: The party officer enforcing voting discipline in Parliament bears the same name as the lash he does not wield.

clue.text: Comedian — Will telly cook his goose? It might

parts.note: Will Hay was a British comic actor of the 1930s
box is slang for television

explanation.surface: Will the comedian be ruined by television? Possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: A haybox is an insulated box packed with hay in which food finishes cooking slowly; 'cook his goose' means ruin him.
explanation.definitionFit: A haybox is a fireless cooker that could literally cook a goose.

clue.text: Game likely to be lost-by the hot-tempered

definitions.meaning: a card game for one player

definitions.text: likely to be lost-by the hot-tempered
definitions.meaning: the quality of calm forbearance that short-tempered people lose

explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a solo card game and also the calm forbearance hot-heads lack.

clue.text: Donated pounds to provide equipment for auctioneer

parts.note: donated means gave
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Money was handed over to buy an auctioneer some kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer bangs a small hammer to close each sale.

clue.text: Innovative work for plough

definitions.meaning: literally, a plough's job is to break up the soil

explanation.definitionFit: Groundbreaking means pioneering, and literally describes the plough breaking up soil.

clue.text: Organist may attempt, it without pay

definitions.meaning: an organ solo played before or after a church service

explanation.definitionFit: A voluntary is an organ piece played in church; voluntary work is unpaid.

clue.text: Boy gets hold of map depicting Arctic region

indicators.note: the boy grips the map within himself

parts.note: a boy is a lad
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A boy clutches a chart of the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is the northern region of Scandinavia, largely within the Arctic Circle.

clue.text: New England communist possible victim of battery

parts.note: Rhode Island is one of the six New England states
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A Bostonian Marxist may have been assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battery' is a battery farm of caged hens, not assault; the answer is a breed of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: This hen breed is commonly kept in battery farms, so it could fall victim to one.

clue.text: Seize the opportunity to produce fodder

definitions.meaning: an idiom, from making the most of sunshine while it lasts
literally, to cut and dry grass as animal feed

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to exploit a chance, from farmers drying grass while the sun shines.

clue.text: Drab kind of desk with time switch

indicators.note: the letter for time changes position within the desk's name

parts.note: a roll-top is a desk with a sliding slatted cover

explanation.surface: A dull type of writing desk gets a timing switch fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drab' is an old noun for a slovenly woman, not the adjective. 'switch' moves the T of ROLLTOP to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab is an archaic noun for a slatternly or immoral woman, a synonym.

clue.text: Loved touring city's arena

indicators.note: touring means moving about, so the letters of loved wander into a new order

parts.note: the city is Rome; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A tourist adored travelling round the city's stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' looks like the tourist's activity but is the anagram signal; VELOD is the rearranged fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is an arena with a banked track for cycle racing.

clue.text: Grandma not quite finishing two pieces of bread?

indicators.note: the last letter of the doubled bread is dropped

parts.note: naan is Indian flatbread, here spelt nan, twice

explanation.surface: Granny leaves a bit of her pair of flatbreads uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite finishing' removes the final N of NANNAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanna is an affectionate family word for a grandmother.

clue.text: Behave without restraint on the French excursion

parts.note: le is French for the
an excursion is a trip

explanation.surface: Someone goes wild on a day out in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for acting or speaking without holding back.

clue.text: Kind of sketch represented in thin album

indicators.note: represented means presented afresh, so the letters of thin album are set out again

explanation.surface: A little drawing appears in a slim book of pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail sketch is a small, quick, rough drawing or description.

clue.text: Black Rod invested in fish, in case

indicators.note: the black rod is clothed or placed inside the fish

parts.note: the scad is a horse mackerel
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
a bar is a rod

explanation.surface: The parliamentary official Black Rod is wrapped in a fish, for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Rod is a ceremonial officer of the House of Lords, but here the phrase is split into B and BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath or case for a sword.

clue.text: Permanently in favour of strongholds

parts.note: for means in favour of
keeps are castle strongholds

explanation.surface: Someone backs castles for good.
explanation.definitionFit: For keeps is an idiom meaning for ever, permanently.

clue.text: In Jerusalem, from a variety of sources select menial

indicators.note: the selecting word is placed inside the name for the holy city

parts.note: Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, a name for Jerusalem

parts.words: from a variety of sources select
parts.note: to cull is to select or gather from several places

explanation.surface: Someone in Jerusalem picks a servant from many candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a kitchen servant doing the most menial work.

clue.text: Cold meal brought round in foil

indicators.note: the meal is placed around the cold letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A chilled dinner is served wrapped in kitchen foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' is the verb meaning thwart, not kitchen wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to thwart or foil it.

clue.text: Good doctor has to begin to work outside state

indicators.note: the verb for coming together goes round the state

parts.note: a plan that jells starts to take shape and work
KY is the abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A kindly doctor must start practising outside a particular state.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Jekyll is the good side of Stevenson's Jekyll and Hyde.
explanation.definitionFit: In Stevenson's tale, Dr Jekyll is the respectable doctor whose evil alter ego is Mr Hyde.

clue.text: Foolish person ruined in a cult

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of in a cult are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone silly is destroyed by membership of a sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic is used loosely of anyone wildly foolish.

clue.text: Crowd limit that's old hat

parts.note: a mob is a crowd
a cap is an upper limit

explanation.surface: A ceiling on crowd numbers is no longer fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like the idiom for outdated; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobcap is a large frilled cotton bonnet worn indoors by women in past centuries.

clue.text: Pope putting interdiction on old city

indicators.note: the ban is placed after the city's name

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
an interdiction is a ban

explanation.surface: A pope imposes an interdict on an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is the name taken by eight popes, including Urban II.

clue.text: Fell very low

definitions.meaning: to fell is to strike down to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: To knock down is to fell someone; a knock-down price is very low.

clue.text: A rope knotted by Billy Budd, for instance

indicators.note: knotted means tied up in tangles, so the letters of a rope are twisted around

explanation.surface: A sailor in Melville's story ties a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Budd is a Melville sailor tale, here meaning Britten's opera of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Britten's Billy Budd is an example of an opera.

clue.text: I repair damaged grassland

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters of I repair are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone vows to fix ruined pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide stretch of grassland in North America.

clue.text: Some entertainment, as soon as king entered court

indicators.note: the phrase goes inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: once means as soon as, as in once he arrived
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A show begins the moment the monarch arrives at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert is a musical performance, a kind of entertainment.

clue.text: Sport was first to be strictly controlled

parts.note: RU is rugby union
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A game was the first to come under strict regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ruled is to be governed or kept under strict control.

clue.text: Thirty days with the family …

definitions.meaning: the usual short form of the ninth month, which has thirty days
a clan or branch of a family, especially in Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: Sept abbreviates the thirty-day ninth month and is also a word for a clan.

clue.text: … refuse to take less than a month

indicators.note: the month is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: March is a month

explanation.surface: Someone declines to accept under a month's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' is the noun (waste), not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is the refuse of grapes or other fruit left after pressing.
